unit.name: Why deep learning won and where CS230 fits
unit.description: Introduces the flipped course format, motivates deep learning through scaling, and places deep learning inside a broader CS, ML, and GenAI stack.
unit.summary: Ng opens by explaining the flipped format and asks students to use live class time for richer questioning rather than passive replay of recorded content [ts=35s] [ts=88s]. He motivates the subject by contrasting older ML methods that plateau with more data against neural networks that continue improving as size, data, and compute scale [ts=198s] [ts=276s]. He ties this to early GPU/CUDA work, later scaling-law predictability, and the investment logic behind modern large models [ts=301s] [ts=402s]. He then situates the course inside a CS fundamentals -> machine learning -> deep learning -> generative AI stack, noting that in practice neural networks and deep learning are nearly interchangeable and that transformers are the GenAI architecture students will later study [ts=450s] [ts=617s].

key_points.text: CS230 uses a flipped classroom format so in-person time can focus on richer discussion.
Traditional ML methods often plateau as data grows, while larger neural networks keep improving with more data and compute.
Scaling laws make deep learning performance more predictable as compute and data increase.
Deep learning sits on top of machine learning and CS fundamentals, and modern GenAI sits on top of deep learning through transformers.
